chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Al-Minqari, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from Ammar Al-Duhni, who said:
I heard Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, Allah loves every grieving heart, and He loves every grateful servant.'

Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, will say to one of His servants on the Day of Judgment: 'Did you thank so-and-so?' He will say, 'No, I thanked You, O Lord.' He will say, 'You did not thank Me because you did not thank him.'
Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'The most thankful to Allah are those who are most thankful to the people.'
ai.seo_question: What is the connection between thanking God and thanking people in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia concept of 'shukr al-ni‘am' by linking divine love to both the humility of a grieving heart and the practical gratitude shown to fellow humans. It highlights that true thankfulness to God is incomplete without acknowledging the intermediaries of His blessings, a principle rooted in the Prophet’s saying, 'The most grateful to people is the most grateful to God.' This underscores the social dimension of worship, where recognizing human agency is an act of recognizing Divine providence.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Al Minqary, from Sufyan Bin Uyayna, from Ammad Al Duhny who said,
‘I heard Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Loves every grieving heart, and Loves every grateful servant.

Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would be Saying to a servant from His<sup>azwj</sup> servant on the Day of Judgement: “Did you thank so and so?” He would say, ‘But, I thanked You<sup>azwj</sup>, O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>!” So He<sup>azwj</sup> would be Saying: “You did not thank Me<sup>azwj</sup> when you did not thank him”.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The most thankful to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, is the one most thankful you to the people’.
en.sarwar: 30. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from al-Minqari from Sufyan ibn ‘Uyayna from ‘Ammar al-Dihni who has said the following:
“Allah loves every sad heart and He loves every thankful servant.

Allah, the Most Blessed, the Most High, on the Day of Judgment will say to a servant among His servants, ‘Did you thank so and so?’ He (that servant) will say, ‘No, but 1 thanked You, O Lord.’ Allah will say, ‘You have not thanked Me because you did not thank him.’
The Imam said, ‘The most thankful among you to Allah is the most thankful among you to people.’”
